subject: Throughput backpressure mitigation — sprint plan & customer-ready digest
messages:
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-28T09:12:34-07:00
Subject: [INCIDENT] FlowMart: sustained throughput backpressure (p95 unchanged, tail throughput drop)

Heads-up — we started seeing sustained backpressure for FlowMart’s API pool around 08:55 PDT. Symptoms: steady p95 latency but 30-40% drop in completed requests/sec for gen endpoints (v2). No obvious host OOMs; a few instances show high scheduler queue depth and increased VK cache eviction.

What we know:
- First delta at ~08:52; reproduction on staging when replaying small spike.
- Autoscaler did not spin up additional nodes; investigating scale thresholds.
- Canary shows worker threads stuck in short schedule loops (attaching canary metrics).

Immediate asks: SRE to triage kernel scheduling and autoscaler gating (Ben, Dylan). Product to help draft short customer note with mitigation steps and ETA (Chloe, Marissa). CS to prep FlowMart ops contact (Rachel).

Attachments: canary_metrics.png (snapshot), flowmart_heap_dump.txt (14KB stub).

Dylan
SRE
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-28T10:03:18-07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] FlowMart: sustained throughput backpressure (p95 unchanged, tail throughput drop)

Thanks — quick tech note. I pulled the host-level traces: three worker processes on the affected pool are reporting high kernel preemption (context-switch churn) aligned with heavy kv-cache writes. Hypothesis: a small fraction of requests are triggering large KV writes (cache update path) that block batching windows and cause downstream queueing.

Mitigation candidates (short list):
- Flip the lightweight KV-write guard to synchronous drop for certain cache-update ops (fast, low risk).
- Temporarily raise autoscaler sensitivity thresholds to allow node add within 60s.
- Apply a canary roll that reduces max batch size for FlowMart’s model variant.

I can implement the autoscaler tweak and the KV guard in ~45–90 mins. If product wants the lower-risk customer note option, we should communicate that we’ve enabled additional capacity and reduced aggressive cache writes.

Ben
Infra Eng
From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-28T11:12:42-07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] FlowMart: sustained throughput backpressure (p95 unchanged, tail throughput drop)

Thanks — good diagnostic. Action plan proposal (short sprint):
1) Ben: apply autoscaler sensitivity bump + enable KV-write guard (target: roll in 60–90 mins).
2) Dylan: confirm that enabling autoscale immediately increases available vCPUs without unsafe fallback. Keep SRE bridge open.
3) Marissa/Karthik: decide on model-variant batch-size rollback if we see no improvement after step 1.
4) Rachel/CS: send concise ops note to FlowMart (1–2 bullets, no apology engineering-dump).

Customer note draft (please comment):
Subject: Brief update: transient capacity constraint affecting throughput
Hi Elaine — we’re seeing reduced throughput on a subset of gen requests this morning. We’ve enabled additional capacity and are applying a targeted fix; you should see traffic restored within the hour. We’ll follow up with a short incident summary and any config changes.

Do we want to include an ETA window (we can say ~60–90 mins)? I prefer to set expectations and follow-up with specifics.

Chloe
Product Manager
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-28T12:05:09-07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] FlowMart: sustained throughput backpressure (p95 unchanged, tail throughput drop)

I reviewed the customer context: FlowMart runs a latency-sensitive checkout pipeline with aggressive concurrency; they recently bumped concurrency by 2x last week (per Rachel). We should call out that this is correlated in the note but avoid assigning blame. Suggest the note say: "we observed a capacity pressure event correlated with increased concurrency and applied capacity and configuration changes to restore throughput."

Also: roadmap ask — if this pattern repeats we should prioritize two things on the short-term roadmap: finer-grained KV write rate-limiting per customer, and a lighter-weight at-runtime batch cap per model variant. I'll add both as backlog items and tag them RED-1452.

Marissa
Head of Product

Cc: ops@flowmart.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

- What we did: enabled additional capacity and applied a targeted scheduler guard to reduce KV write contention.
- What to expect: you should see normal throughput returning; if you still observe errors or high latency in the next 60–90 minutes please reply and we’ll escalate immediately.

We’ll send a short incident summary once we verify stability.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
